about: An original bilingual benchmark: English written for this file, with several
acceptable Persian renderings each. Rights-clean on purpose — no published
translation is quoted — which is also its limit: it measures translation, not
Each case names the one thing it is about. A translation that gets that thing
right passes, in any of the accepted forms; the variants exist because there
is never one correct Persian sentence, and a benchmark that demands one is
measuring agreement with its author instead of fidelity.
`fails` is the other half and the reason the file is useful: a plausible,
fluent rendering that changes the meaning. Those are the ones structural QA
cannot see — they have the right length, the right markers and the right

cases.source: She did not refuse the invitation, though she waited a day to answer.
accepts: او دعوت را رد نکرد، هرچند یک روز برای پاسخ صبر کرد.
دعوت را رد نکرد، اگرچه یک روز تا جواب دادن صبر کرد.

fails.text: او دعوت را نپذیرفت، هرچند یک روز برای پاسخ صبر کرد.
fails.why: «نپذیرفت» is *did not accept*; the source says she did not refuse. Same length, same register, opposite fact.

cases.rationale: Double negation is the commonest silent inversion, and nothing downstream can see it: the sentence is fluent and the length ratio is perfect.

cases.source: The lawyer paid the clerk, and neither of them mentioned the letter.
accepts: وکیل به منشی پول داد و هیچ‌یک از آن دو به نامه اشاره نکرد.
وکیل پول را به منشی پرداخت و هیچ‌کدام نامی از نامه نبردند.

fails.text: منشی به وکیل پول داد و هیچ‌یک از آن دو به نامه اشاره نکرد.
fails.why: Payer and payee are swapped. Persian word order makes this easy to do and invisible to every count.

cases.rationale: Who did what to whom survives no structural check at all.

cases.source: The men who had signed the petition were dismissed.
accepts: مردانی که طومار را امضا کرده بودند اخراج شدند.
آن مردانی که پای طومار را امضا کرده بودند از کار برکنار شدند.

fails.text: مردان، که طومار را امضا کرده بودند، اخراج شدند.
fails.why: The comma turns a restrictive clause into a parenthetical: now *all* the men were dismissed, and the signing is an aside. One punctuation mark, a different fact.

cases.rationale: Restrictive versus non-restrictive is carried by punctuation in both languages and is the easiest thing to normalise away while tidying.

cases.source: By the time the letter arrived, she had already left the house.
accepts: وقتی نامه رسید، او پیش‌تر از خانه رفته بود.
تا نامه برسد، او دیگر خانه را ترک کرده بود.

fails.text: وقتی نامه رسید، او از خانه رفت.
fails.why: The past perfect is flattened to a simple past, so the departure now happens *after* the letter arrives. The whole point of the sentence is the order.

cases.rationale: Persian marks the pluperfect with «بود»; dropping it is grammatical and reverses the sequence.

cases.source: Fewer than half the houses on the street still had their old doors.
accepts: کمتر از نیمی از خانه‌های آن خیابان هنوز درهای قدیمی خود را داشتند.
در کمتر از نصف خانه‌های خیابان، درهای قدیمی هنوز سر جایشان بود.

fails.text: بیش از نیمی از خانه‌های آن خیابان هنوز درهای قدیمی خود را داشتند.
fails.why: «بیش از» is *more than*. A number that reads naturally is not a number that is right.

cases.rationale: Quantities and comparatives invert without changing length, register or vocabulary.

cases.source: He let the matter drop, which cost him nothing and bought him a year.
accepts: موضوع را رها کرد؛ کاری که برایش هیچ هزینه‌ای نداشت و یک سال برایش خرید.
قضیه را کنار گذاشت — چیزی از او کم نکرد و یک سال به او داد.

fails.text: او موضوع را انداخت، که برایش هیچ هزینه‌ای نداشت و یک سال خرید.
fails.why: «انداخت» translates *drop* literally: he threw the matter. The English idiom means he stopped pursuing it.

cases.rationale: A literal rendering of an idiom is the failure that most looks like diligence.

cases.source: — Charming, said the colonel, who had never once been charmed.
accepts: — دلرباست، سرهنگ گفت؛ سرهنگی که یک بار هم دلش نرفته بود.
— چه دلپذیر، سرهنگ گفت، که هرگز از چیزی خوشش نیامده بود.

fails.text: سرهنگ با خوشحالی گفت: بسیار جذاب است! او همیشه از این چیزها لذت می‌برد.
fails.why: The irony is removed and replaced with its opposite. Fluent, warm, and the character is gone.

cases.rationale: Irony is the thing a smoothing pass destroys first, and no count can see it.

cases.source: He smiled, then left without a word, closing the door behind him.
accepts: لبخند زد و بی‌آنکه چیزی بگوید رفت و در را پشت سرش بست.
لبخندی زد، بعد بی هیچ حرفی رفت و در را بست.

fails.text: لبخند زد و رفت و در را بست.
fails.why: «بی‌آنکه چیزی بگوید» is gone. The sentence is shorter, fluent, and the silence — the point — has been deleted.

cases.rationale: A dropped subordinate clause and a terser style look identical to a length ratio.
